source.title: Unveiling Multi-regime Patterns in SciML: Distinct Failure Modes and Regime-specific Optimization
source.authors: Yu-Xin Wang; Yuanzhe Hu; Xiaokun Zhong; Xiaopeng Wang; Haiquan Lu; Tian-Yu Pang; Michael W. Mahoney; Yujun Yan; Pu Ren; Yao-Qing Yang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests train/test error regimes and how SciML training settings affect them, while arguing that training loss can misrepresent test performance and that generalization failure persists under interventions. Its experiments are in scientific machine learning rather than the claim's natural-label classification settings.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported SciML training/test-error regime results and the measured relationship between training loss and test error. Results cited from prior work are not included. The study does not test arbitrary-label memorization or most named claim-version conditions.
record.test_reason: The study reports SciML optimization and generalization regimes, but none of its results tests V1–V8. Low training loss with high test error does not test random-label memorization, width effects, or the specified training interventions. Its Hessian measurements concern curvature and trainability, rather than V7's magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization-gap ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report recurring descriptive three-regime patterns across the examined SciML settings, regime-specific intervention effectiveness, and landscape geometries that complicate standard interpretations of curvature and optimization stability.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SciML PDE/ODE learning, varying physical difficulty, supervision, and training interventions; it does not reproduce the arbitrary-label memorization or natural-label generalization experiments in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Regime geometry and trainability/generalization boundaries vary with model family, physical system, supervision level, and optimization or training strategy; interventions can shift boundaries while leaving generalization-limited regions.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five SciML model families, physical difficulty and supervision produce recurring low-loss/low-error, high-loss/high-error, and low-loss/high-error regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SciML training loss can fail to indicate solution fidelity, with failure regimes depending on physical difficulty and supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: Stabilization, constraint enforcement, curricula, and NNCG fine-tuning change regime boundaries or improve selected settings while leaving failures elsewhere.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SciML training interventions have regime-dependent effectiveness and can improve trainability without eliminating generalization failure.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian curvature can increase as training loss falls, and low-curvature regions can retain high training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian sharpness alone does not reliably characterize trainability in the examined SciML tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 306, 2026.
record.problems: The paper says the representative model-family evaluations are not strictly controlled architecture ablations. Regime heatmaps are seed-averaged and normalized independently by subplot, and many per-condition outcomes are conveyed as plots rather than tabulated values. The SciML test tasks do not address the claim's natural-label classification or arbitrary-label memorization conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were left out; selected regime and loss-landscape findings are represented by the rows above. Exact per-cell heatmap values are not reconstructed from figures.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including switching and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that mitigate them.
Dropout effects, small-data and excessive-dropout conditions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern related findings outside the specified versions; their exclusion rests on missing experimental contrasts and measures, not merely the SciML domain. Regime thresholds are configuration-dependent and subplot colors are independently normalized, so the maps do not establish common absolute performance levels across methods or model families.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label classification comparison.
No width sweep or test-error analysis beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on image classification.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison on image or language benchmarks.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness comparison or ranking against norm- and margin-based generalization measures.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Swept the 1D convection coefficient and collocation-point count; reported training loss and test error regimes.
rows.measure: Training loss and test error jointly classified into well-trained, under-trained and over-trained regimes.
rows.value: The paper reports low training loss with low test error in Regime I, high training and test errors in Regime II, and low training error with high test error in Regime III.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; regime thresholds perturbed by ±20% for robustness analysis.
rows.note: Regime results concern PDE solution fidelity and test error on the paper's SciML task, not natural-label classification.
rows.check: The reported SciML regimes are supported, but they do not measure any claim version; observed is not a version-relative state.

rows.measure: Training loss and test error jointly classified into three regimes.
rows.value: The paper reports low training loss with low test error in Regime I, high training and test errors in Regime II, and low training error with high test error in Regime III.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; regime thresholds perturbed by ±20% for robustness analysis.
rows.note: The reported task is PDE operator learning; its test errors do not establish the claim's natural-label setting.
rows.check: Operator-learning training/test regimes do not measure any claim version.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Compared regime maps across four PDE systems under a fixed PINN architecture and optimizer.
rows.measure: Joint training-loss and test-error regime structure.
rows.value: All four PDEs show recurring regions for stable training and generalization, optimization difficulty, and degraded generalization; their boundary geometry and location vary.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; exact per-setting values are shown as regime plots.
rows.note: This compares physical systems, not image classification architectures.
rows.check: Recurring regimes across PDE systems do not test any specified version.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Compared RoPINN regime map with the L-BFGS setting and reported changes in trainability and generalization regions.
rows.value: RoPINN shifts the trainability boundary toward larger β but leaves the generalization-limited regime visible, especially with low collocation or high β.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; exact per-setting values are shown as regime plots.
rows.note: The intervention improves trainability without eliminating generalization failure.
rows.check: RoPINN's stabilization effects do not measure a specified version; partial describes intervention effectiveness rather than a claim-version effect.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Changed constraint enforcement from a soft-constraint penalty method to hard-constrained ALM and compared regime boundaries.
rows.baseline: Soft-constrained PINN training; training-loss transition at β ≈ 25
rows.value: ALM shifts the training-loss transition to β ≈ 50 and expands portions of the trainable region; it does not remove Regime III.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; exact per-setting values are shown as regime plots.
rows.note: The reported intervention changes constraint handling and regime boundaries.
rows.check: The approximately 25-to-50 transition shift is supported, but constraint enforcement is outside V1–V8.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Progressively increased PDE coefficient during training and compared regime boundaries and generalization-gap behavior.
rows.measure: Training-loss and test-error regime boundaries; likelihood of a high generalization gap.
rows.baseline: ALM regime map for the stated comparison
rows.value: CL shifts the Regime I/II boundary toward harder physical parameters and lower-data settings; it reduces the likelihood of a high generalization gap in parts of Regime III but does not fully remove generalization-limited behavior.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; exact per-setting values are shown as regime plots.
rows.note: The paper describes smoother transitions and improved accuracy in selected regions.
rows.check: Curriculum learning's regime-boundary and test-error effects do not test a specified version.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.stage_stated: L-BFGS solution followed by NNCG fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Applied NNCG as post-training fine-tuning and compared relative training-loss and test-error performance with L-BFGS.
rows.measure: Relative improvement in training loss and test error over L-BFGS.
rows.value: In Regime I, NNCG reduces test error by approximately 50% in data-limited scenarios and improves training loss by roughly 60% in well-trained scenarios; in high-β Regime II, averaged performance shows minimal improvement and individual runs often encounter numerical instability or divergence.
rows.uncertainty: Average over three random seeds; unstable or divergent runs are included.
rows.note: This is a comparison of training methods in SciML; the text states the numerical gains approximately.
rows.check: The approximate 50% test-error and 60% training-loss improvements are supported. This NNCG/L-BFGS comparison does not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison or another version.

rows.subject: FNO
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss and Hessian sharpness across FNO settings and examined their relation to test error.

conditions.value: training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue across regime configurations

rows.measure: Relationship between training loss and Hessian sharpness, with test-error regime context.
rows.value: Some higher Hessian metric values occur in well-trained regions, while lower values characterize poorly trained regions; the paper states that sharpness alone does not reliably characterize trainability quality.
rows.note: This does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps as V7 specifies.
rows.check: Correctly excluded from V7: unscaled Hessian eigenvalues and trainability comparisons do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps at similarly low training loss.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue through optimization.
rows.measure: Training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue over epochs.
rows.value: The maximum Hessian eigenvalue rises sharply during the initial phase, coinciding with the rapid decay in training loss; both stabilize later.
rows.note: A within-training correlation in a SciML task; not a measure of the V7 generalization gap.
rows.check: Within-training curvature/loss dynamics do not measure V7's between-network generalization-gap association.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss and Hessian eigenvalues across reaction-diffusion physical settings.
rows.measure: Training loss and Hessian eigenvalue/landscape characteristics.
rows.value: The ρ = 5 setting has a sharper minimum and larger Hessian eigenvalues after training but better optimization performance; the flatter ρ = 15 landscape has broad high-loss plateaus and weaker descent structure.
rows.note: The comparison addresses optimization quality and training loss; it does not measure V7's magnitude-aware gap association.
rows.check: The sharper, better-optimized setting is supported, but unequal training losses and unscaled Hessian measurements do not test V7.

rows.subject: PINN
rows.size_stated: MLP with four hidden layers; hidden dimensions [50, 50, 50, 50].
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss and test error along a Bezier curve connecting coarse-convergence L-BFGS and fine-convergence ALM checkpoints.

conditions.value: L-BFGS coarse convergence L ≈ 10−2; ALM fine convergence L ≈ 10−4

rows.measure: Training loss and test error along the checkpoint-interpolating Bezier curve.
rows.value: The two checkpoints lie within the same basin according to training loss, but their test errors differ significantly; the coarse checkpoint has low training loss and large test error, while further optimization is needed for physically accurate solutions.
rows.note: This directly shows a training/test discrepancy in a SciML PDE task, outside the claim's stated natural-label classification scope.
rows.check: The stage should include both the L-BFGS coarse checkpoint and ALM fine checkpoint, plus their connecting curve. The training-loss/test-error discrepancy does not measure a specified version.
